questions.question: Identify the correct statement. सही कथन की पहचान कीजिए।
questions.solution:
The SI unit of power is Watt (W) which is joules per second (J/s). Sometimes the power of motor vehicles and other machines is given in terms of Horsepower (hp), which is approximately equal to 745.7 watts.

The joule is the unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI). newton, absolute unit of force in the International System of Units (SI units), abbreviated N. It is defined as that force necessary to provide a mass of one kilogram with an acceleration of one metre per second per second.

• Joule (J) - SI unit of energy.

• Calorie (cal) - A unit of energy used in nutrition.

• Kilowatt-hour (kWh) - A unit of electrical energy.

• Newton (N) - SI unit of force, not energy.

questions.solution:
Let's analyze each statement:

· Light year is a unit of distance. This is correct. A light-year is used to measure astronomical distances.

· Light is a unit of time. This is incorrect. "Light" itself is electromagnetic radiation. "Year" is a unit of time, but "light-year" is a unit of distance.

· A light year is the distance that light travels in one Earth year. This is the correct definition of a light-year. Light travels at approximately 299,792 kilometers per second (or about 9.46 trillion kilometers in a year).

· Light year is the measurement of light intensity. This is incorrect. Light intensity is typically measured in units like candela or lux.

Therefore, statements I and III are correct.

Further insights:

• A light-year is a very large unit of distance, suitable for expressing distances to stars and galaxies.

• For example, Proxima Centauri, the nearest star to our Sun, is about 4.24 light-years away.

• The concept helps in understanding the vast scales of the universe.

questions.question: What is the unit of work done? किए गए कार्य की इकाई क्या है?
questions.solution: The unit of work done is the joule (J) in the International System of Units (SI). The joule is defined as the amount of work done when a force of one newton is applied over a distance of one meter in the direction of the force.
1 horsepower (hp) is equivalent to 746 watts (approximately 750 watts), which is a unit of power.

questions.question: Coulomb per second is equivalent to ______. कूलम्ब प्रति सेकंड ______ के बराबर है।
questions.solution:
Coulomb Per Second (C/s) is a unit in the category of Electric current. It is also known as coulombs per second, coulomb/second. This unit is commonly used in the SI unit system. Coulomb Per Second (C/s) has a dimension of I where I is electric current. It is essentially the same as the corresponding standard SI unit A.

The physical quantity coulomb/second is referred to as the ampere in the scientific community.

An ampere is a unit of measure of the rate of electron flow or current in an electrical conductor. One ampere of current represents one coulomb of electrical charge (6.24 x 1018 charge carriers) moving past a specific point in one second.

The physical quantity for the expression of arc/radius is the Plane angle. A plane angle is well known: one full revolution is 360° or 2π radians.

The solid angle expands this concept over the surface of a sphere. The solid angle as seen from the centre of a sphere, includes a given area on the surface of that sphere.

questions.question: What is the power of 'second' in the SI unit of acceleration? त्वरण की SI इकाई में 'सेकंड' का घात कितना है?
questions.solution: The meter per second squared (symbolized m/s 2 or m/sec 2 ) is the Standard International (SI) unit of acceleration vector magnitude. This quantity can be defined in either of two senses: average or instantaneous. The SI unit of acceleration is meters/second2 (m/s2). Hence, the power of the second is -2 as it is in the denominator.

questions.question: What is the unit of specific resistance? विशिष्ट प्रतिरोध की इकाई क्या है?
questions.solution:
Specific resistance (also called resistivity) is a material property that quantifies how strongly a given material opposes the flow of electric current.

· The formula for resistivity (ρ) is:

ρ=R*L/A

​

where:

o R = resistance (in ohms)

o A = cross-sectional area (in square meters)

o L = length (in meters)

· The unit of resistivity is Ohm meter (Ω·m).

Thus, option 4 is correct.

questions.question: The SI unit of speed is. चाल का SI मात्रक _________ है।
questions.solution: Different objects may take different amounts of time to cover a given distance. Some of them move fast and some move slowly. The rate at which objects move can be different. Also, different objects can move at the same rate. One of the ways of measuring the rate of motion of an object is to find out the distance travelled by the object in unit time. This quantity is referred to as speed. The SI unit of speed is metre per second. This is represented by the symbol m s - 1 or m/s. The other units of speed include centimetre per second (cm s - 1) and kilometre per hour (km h - 1).

The diopter is the standard unit for measuring the optical power of lenses. It represents the reciprocal of the focal length in meters and is crucial in optics and ophthalmology for describing lens strength.

• Magnetic intensity (H) in the CGS system is measured in Oersted, representing the strength of the magnetic field.

• Gauss measures magnetic flux density (B), not intensity. Candela and weber are unrelated units.

Further Insight:

· In the SI system, magnetic intensity is measured in amperes per meter, replacing Oersted in modern usage.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of current? वर्तमान की SI इकाई क्या है?
questions.solution: The SI unit of electric current is the Ampere (A), named after the French scientist André-Marie Ampère. It measures the rate of flow of electric charge in a circuit.

Joule: unit of heat

Ohm: unit of resistance

Ampere: unit of current-flow

Volt: unit of voltage of potential difference

options.text: C= A X 2s C= A X 2s
options.html: C= A X 2sC= A X 2s

questions.solution:
The ampere (A) is the SI unit of electric current. Electric current is defined as the rate of flow of electric charge. One ampere is defined as the flow of one coulomb (C) of charge per second (s).

Therefore, the relationship is: 1 Ampere (A) = 1 Coulomb (C) / 1 second (s), or A = C/s.

So, option (1) A=1C/s correctly represents this definition.

Further insights:

• The formal definition of the ampere was revised in 2019 and is now based on fixing the numerical value of the elementary charge 'e' (the charge of a proton or electron). However, the practical understanding and relationship A = C/s remain fundamental.

• Electric charge (Q) is measured in coulombs, current (I) in amperes, and time (t) in seconds. The formula relating them is Q = I X t, or I = Q / t.
